docs.title: Book Structure
docs.text: This book consists of ten chapters organized across four levels (Figure 0-2). Chapter 1 establishes the foundational framework for Agents; Chapters 2 through 6 discuss how to build Agents, covering context, knowledge, tools, code generation, and interaction in sequence; Chapters 7 through 9 discuss how to evaluate and continuously improve Agents, progressing from measurement systems and model post-training to continuous evolution driven by operational experience; Chapter 10 broadens the scope to multi-agent collaboration.

docs.title: Agent = LLM + Context + Tools
docs.text: The Core Formula The core formula of the book: the LLM is the brain (decision-making), context is the eyes (what it can see), and tools are the hands and feet (what it can do). In academic terms this maps to policy, observation space, and action space; in production form it expands to Agent = Model + Harness.

docs.title: Harness
docs.text: Harness The runtime and governance layer inside the agent boundary, beyond the model: context management + tool interfaces + constraints + verification + correction. The model is a powerful but unpredictable horse; the harness channels that power in the right direction.

docs.title: ReAct Loop
docs.text: ReAct Loop The core execution pattern of an agent: an iterative loop of Reasoning → Acting → Observing. By continuously appending to the trajectory, the model keeps pushing the task forward until it is done.

docs.title: Context Engineering
docs.text: Context Engineering The engineering discipline of systematically designing, organizing, and supplying all background knowledge an AI needs to complete a task. Context quality caps agent capability — a mid-tier model with well-organized context often beats a top model groping through information scarcity.

docs.title: KV Cache
docs.text: KV Cache The inference-engine mechanism that caches computed key-value pairs of tokens to avoid recomputation. Core constraint: change one byte of the prefix and everything cached after the first differing token is invalidated — so once the system prompt is settled, never change it; dynamic information always appends to the end.

docs.title: Static Prefix + Trajectory
docs.text: Static Prefix + Trajectory A model of context composition: system prompt + tool definitions form the immutable static prefix of a conversation, while user messages + model replies + tool results form the dynamically growing trajectory. This is the common foundation of KV Cache optimization and context compression.

docs.title: Agent Skills
docs.text: Agent Skills Packaging domain capability as modular, load-on-demand knowledge bundles: the SKILL.md metadata catalog stays resident in context, the full body loads only when selected, and file references can reach deeper sub-documents. The canonical form of progressive disclosure.

docs.title: Progressive Disclosure
docs.text: Progressive Disclosure Instead of putting everything into context at once, first provide a searchable catalog, then load details on demand. Optimizes both the context budget and selection precision; Skills, hierarchical retrieval, and active tool discovery are all variants of it.

docs.title: Agent Status Bar
docs.text: Agent Status Bar A structured state summary continuously injected at the end of context (task progress, tool-call counters, environment info), distilling implicit state scattered across the trajectory into explicitly retrievable knowledge. Experiments show small models with a status bar can approach frontier large models.

docs.title: Context Rot
docs.text: Context Rot The context still fits but can no longer be found: as irrelevant content grows, attention dilutes and retrieval precision of key information degrades. Unlike context overflow (it doesn't fit), rot is stealthier — the agent appears to work fine while decision quality quietly slides.

docs.title: Proposer–Reviewer
docs.text: Proposer-Reviewer Production and judgment are carried by two roles that share no context; the reviewer sees the artifact itself, not the reasoning process. It holds because self-review is unreliable; used for safety approval, content iteration, evaluation UIs, and update-proposal review.

docs.title: Sidecar
docs.text: Sidecar A lightweight LLM call running in parallel with the main model's streaming output that looks only at structured data (e.g., JSON fields of tool calls) for safety checks or context construction — never at free text, to prevent manipulation through injected rhetoric.

docs.title: MCP
docs.text: Model Context Protocol Anthropic's open standard for model–tool interoperability: three primitive types (tools, resources, prompts) over stdio / Streamable HTTP transports. It solves build-once-use-everywhere, but not tool-choice overload — that is what Skills and active tool discovery are for.

docs.title: Prompt Injection
docs.text: Prompt Injection An attack where an adversary plants instruction-like text into context through external content the agent processes, hijacking its behavior. Context-level defenses (source tagging, instruction/data separation) only lower the success rate; the fundamental defense lives at the execution and data layers.

docs.title: RAG
docs.text: Retrieval-Augmented Generation Chunk → dense/sparse retrieval → fusion (RRF) → rerank → generate. Contextual retrieval adds prefix summaries to chunks at index time, cutting retrieval failure rates by 49–67%.

docs.title: User Memory
docs.text: User Memory Cross-session personalized persistent knowledge, in progressively richer formats: Simple Notes → Advanced JSON Cards → executable code (User as Code). Combined with RAG into two-layer memory — structured facts resident, raw details retrieved on demand.

docs.title: Mid-training / SFT / RL
docs.text: Post-training Three stages of capability development: mid-training fills in knowledge and foundational abilities on the target distribution; SFT solidifies formats and protocols with demonstrations (loss computed only on responses); RL maximizes expected reward and explores beyond demonstrations. Decision framework: missing foundation → mid-training, missing protocol → SFT, missing strategy → RL.

docs.title: RLVR 与 RLVP
docs.text: Verifiable Rewards / Penalty RLVR uses executable verification (tests, state assertions) to determine rewards directly; RLVP adds path constraints on top — rewarding outcomes while penalizing verifiably violating paths, restoring learning signal within all-win/all-loss rollout groups.

docs.title: On-Policy Distillation
docs.text: On-Policy Distillation The student samples its own trajectories while the teacher provides per-token distributions at each student state, expanding a rollout's terminal scalar into dense supervision. Matching pure-RL math performance takes roughly 1/10 the training steps.

docs.title: Loop Engineering
docs.text: Loop Engineering Designing the loops that keep an agent running — discover tasks, execute, verify, record — with a verifier, not the model itself, deciding when it may stop. Core consensus: the bottleneck of the loop is the verifier, not the model.

docs.title: Pass@k vs Pass^k
docs.text: Pass@k vs Pass^k Pass@k: the probability of at least one success in k tries — the ceiling of capability (technical spectacle). Pass^k: the probability of k consecutive full successes — business reliability. At p=0.6, Pass@5 ≈ 99% while Pass^5 ≈ 7.8%.

docs.title: LLM-as-a-Judge
docs.text: LLM-as-a-Judge Using an LLM to score open-ended outputs against a rubric. Four criteria: grounded in expert guidance, comprehensive coverage (including pitfalls), importance-weighted (supporting vetoes), and self-contained standards. Guard against length bias and collusion between same-family models.
